description: We are Team Vaarahi, interested in space technology, AI, data science, and web development. We aim to build an interactive application that combines MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire data into a burning activity calendar with maps, charts, and historical analysis. We welcome teammates skilled in Python, web development, data visualization, satellite data, and UI/UX design.
summary:
FireHarmonizer is a near-real-time wildfire monitoring and satellite data analysis platform that integrates NASA FIRMS observations from MODIS and VIIRS satellites. It provides an interactive global map to explore fire hotspots across countries, states, cities and geographic regions.

The platform processes satellite observations using data validation, cross-platform VIIRS deduplication and spatial-temporal matching to identify candidate associations between MODIS and VIIRS detections. It also provides historical fire analysis, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) statistics, anomaly exploration and downloadable reports.

Built using React, TypeScript, Python and FastAPI, FireHarmonizer transforms complex satellite observations into accessible geospatial intelligence through an interactive dashboard. Its goal is to support wildfire monitoring, environmental research and informed disaster-management decisions.
details: FireHarmonizer is a global wildfire monitoring and satellite data harmonization platform that uses NASA FIRMS data from MODIS and VIIRS satellites. It provides an interactive global fire map, location-based search, historical fire analysis, fire activity calendars, anomaly exploration, and downloadable reports. The system validates satellite observations, removes duplicate VIIRS detections across different platforms, and performs spatial-temporal matching between MODIS and VIIRS observations. It also calculates Fire Radiative Power (FRP) statistics for comparative analysis. The application was developed using Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, and Leaflet. Its goal is to make satellite-based wildfire information easier to explore, compare, and understand for research and disaster-response awareness.
